prerequisites: Fundamental concepts of mathematical analysis, physics, mechanics, fluid dynamics, thermodynamics, and electromagnetism.

learning_outcomes.text: Acquire basic knowledge on measurement instrumentation for mechanical and thermal quantities, providing the necessary elements for understanding measurement processes, the interaction between the measurand and the measurement system, the static and dynamic characteristics of measurement systems, uncertainty, the operating principles of sensors and transducers, and their use in laboratory and industrial settings.

Learn, through examples and exercises in the classroom and laboratory, how to plan a measurement process, calibrate instruments, and perform measurements in the context of experimental research, product development, testing of machines and systems, quality and process control, diagnosis and maintenance, and management of production departments, as well as control, verification, and technical assistance activities.
Develop the ability to work in a team, write a report on the activity carried out, and present the work orally and in writing, stimulated by laboratory activities and the development of essays.

syllabus_topics: General notions on the concept of measurement
Application of measurement instrumentation in various industrial sectors, particularly in testing
Characterization of an instrument: calibration, determination of static and dynamic characteristics
Elements of statistics, signal analysis, and data processing, basics for understanding signals in the frequency domain
Traditional and innovative systems for measuring: dimension, displacement, deformation, solid velocity, fluid velocity, acceleration, force, torque, power, pressure, flow rate, temperature
Basic notions on data acquisition systems and signal digitization (sampling, quantization, coding, main devices)
Exercises on signal acquisition and processing with LabView

assessment_methods.method: Discussion of lecture and laboratory practical exercise topics

assessment_rules: The exam consists of an oral test with a discussion of topics from both lectures and practical laboratory exercises. 3 (max 4 if there is doubt about the grade) questions will be asked: one on general metrological characteristics, one on the operating principles of instruments, and one on signal acquisition. The final grade will correspond to the average of the grades obtained on the individual questions, given in thirtieths. The minimum passing grade for the exam is 18/30. A distinction (lode) will be awarded to students who achieve the maximum grade and demonstrate particular mastery of the subject.
